# Results — Study 188 (Head-Shoulders) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Pattern: head-and-shoulders
top (bearish) and inverse head-and-shoulders (bullish) confirmed by a neckline break on

Basket: SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META, NVDA, TSLA, JPM.  Daily bars from
2005-01-03 to 2026-06-15, adjusted close.  As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## The honest test — confirmed neckline break, forward returns vs random baseline

Pattern detection: `scipy.signal.find_peaks` local-extrema logic, shoulder symmetry
tolerance 10%, neckline tilt tolerance 15%, span 20–200 bars, minimum 5-bar extrema
distance.  Signal fires at the close of the neckline break bar; trade entered the next
day's open.  Baseline: random-day forward returns drawn uniformly from the same tape.
Multiple-comparisons correction: Bonferroni over 2 pattern types × 4 horizons = 8 tests
(threshold |t| ~ 2.58).

### H&S top (bearish signal — short entry)

| Horizon | n | mean % | win-rate | HAC t | excess % | t_excess |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day   |  3 | +1.14 | 100% | n/a | +1.12 | n/a |
| 5 days  |  3 | +0.01 |  67% | n/a | −1.07 | n/a |
| 20 days |  3 | +6.17 |  67% | n/a | +7.46 | n/a |
| 60 days |  3 | +9.10 |  33% | n/a | +12.07 | n/a |

**n = 3 across 10 tickers over ~20 years** — the rule fires so rarely that HAC
inference is impossible.  This is itself the result: strict algorithmic detection of the
full five-point structure (left shoulder, neckline trough, head, neckline trough, right
shoulder, confirmed break) produces almost no signals on major US equities.

### Inverse H&S (bullish signal — long entry)

| Horizon | n | mean % | win-rate | HAC t | excess % | t_excess |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day   | 20 | −0.02 | 55% | −0.07 | +0.33 | +0.60 |
| 5 days  | 20 | −0.21 | 40% | −0.60 | −0.54 | −0.53 |
| 20 days | 20 | +0.53 | 65% | +0.54 | −2.41 | −1.97 |
| 60 days | 20 | +2.27 | 65% | +0.96 | −2.19 | −0.77 |

With 20 signals HAC inference is possible but borderline.  No horizon clears the
Bonferroni threshold (max |t_excess| = 1.97 < 2.58).  The 20-day excess is actually
*negative* (inverse H&S underperforms random entries at that horizon), the opposite of
what the pattern predicts.

## Why so few signals?

A strict algorithmic implementation filters out almost every "textbook" H&S because:

1. **Shoulder symmetry**: real markets almost never produce shoulders within 10% of each
   other in height — asymmetric shoulders are the norm, not the exception.
2. **Horizontal neckline**: the standard rule requires an approximately horizontal
   neckline; tilted necklines (common in practice) are excluded.
3. **Confirmed break**: waiting for a confirmed neckline close to fire the signal means
   the move is already largely over — the "measured move" below the neckline rarely
   materialises cleanly.

Studies that find significant results from H&S patterns typically use looser detection
rules (no symmetry constraint, any "similar" shoulder) or look for the pattern
subjectively — which is the textbook selection-bias problem.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** H&S top: n = 3, inference impossible. Inverse H&S: n = 20,
  max |t_excess| = 1.97 (Bonferroni threshold 2.58), not significant.  No horizon or
  pattern type produces a statistically real directional edge over an unconditional
  baseline.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The strict detector fires roughly 0.3 H&S top signals per
  ticker per 20 years — far below any tradable frequency.  Looser detection rules that
  fire more frequently also fire on noise and carry severe selection bias.  Either way,
  the pattern is untradable at a reasonable frequency.
- **Pattern frequency — CONFIRMED too-rare.** The strict rule produces 23 signals in
  200 ticker-years.  The famous "reliability" of H&S in textbooks is an artefact of
  (a) subjective pattern recognition that fires more freely, and (b) publication bias.
